Lanky

LANG-kee · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Lanky is ungracefully thin and tall; gangly.

The lanky basketball recruit was already six foot seven as a high school sophomore, all elbows and knees.

Worked Example

Watching the lanky colt take its first wobbly steps on legs far too long for its body was both awkward and endearing.

Lanky specifically combines height and thinness with a sense of awkwardness -- someone lanky often looks like they haven't quite grown into their own limbs yet.

How Lanky Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

gangly

gangly: awkwardly tall and thin, especially of a young person

rangy

rangy: tall, thin, and long-limbed

Antonyms

stocky

stocky: short and solidly built

burly

burly: large, strong, and muscular

How Strong Is It? — tall → lanky → gawky

tall vs. lanky

tall vs. lanky: Tall just means above-average height, without the thinness or slight awkwardness that lanky implies.

gawky vs. lanky

gawky vs. lanky: Gawky pushes lanky's awkwardness even further, into outright clumsiness.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — lank

root — lank: thin and limp (Old English hlanc, of debated further origin)

suffix — -y

suffix — -y: full of, characterized by (Old English (-ig))

Put it together

Put it together: Lanky is the older English word lank ('thin and limp') plus the adjective ending -y ('characterized by') -- marked by that long, thin limpness. Unlike many of this unit's words, it doesn't branch off into a bigger word family.

Use the root in a new word: lankiness

Use the root in a new word: lankiness: His lankiness made it hard to find dress pants that were both long enough and narrow enough.

Lanky is a purely physical description -- unlike this unit's other words, it says nothing about personality, only about someone's tall, thin, and slightly awkward build.
